result.summary:
I audited App Review Information (packet section 6 at 7b224c5a) against the client source and production. The client source is the build under review: git diff --stat eed0f628 7b224c5a -- SmartCompareApp app landing is empty. Five sentences in the notes are false or would mislead a reviewer.

1. "Scan Product" is not shown anywhere in the build. The home.scan key has no use outside the i18n files.
2. The gallery link reads "Or pick from gallery", not "Pick from gallery". The home.camera.gallery key is not used.
3. "On Home, type two products" leaves out a step. Home opens in Scan mode (HomeScreen.tsx:116), so the reviewer must tap the Type tab first.
4. The "raised daily comparison limit" is false until the owner runs the SQL in finding F06. Premium allows 10 a day and 70 a month (usage_service.py:144-148).
5. The Bahrain sentence claims prices are gathered from retailers across the GCC. Nothing in this audit backs that.

The notes also leave out four things:
- Sign in with Apple only works after the Terms/13+ checkbox is ticked.
- A new Apple account must answer a 16-screen onboarding before it reaches Home.
- A new email account may need to confirm its email first.
- The exact path to account deletion.

These claims check out:
- The AI permission sheet's title and button, and that it gates every text, link, scan, camera-permission and gallery path.
- The gear icon goes to Edit Profile, then Delete account, then the alert's confirm.
- The Bahrain market and BHD.
- No in-app purchases, ads or tracking SDKs.
- 20-40 seconds matches canary 7c (26.9-32.4 s).

Two things need the owner before submission:
- The Google button is in this build, and whether it works is still unchecked.
- Live /health reports Bright Data at status 401, so price coverage is reduced.

ready_text holds the corrected Notes: 3032 bytes, all ASCII, placeholders kept. The tier SQL is in finding F06.

findings.title: "Scan Product" is not on screen
findings.claim: Packet line 285: "Or tap Scan Product to photograph two products".
findings.evidence: In SmartCompareApp/src, home.scan ("Scan Product", en.json:111) appears only in en.json and ar.json. git grep finds no t('home.scan') in any screen. Home shows a mode segment with Scan / Link / Type tabs (HomeScreen.tsx:1002-1038, en.json:710-712). In Scan mode without camera permission it shows "Turn on camera" (home.permission.cta, en.json:715; HomeScreen.tsx:760-764). With permission granted it shows an "Open camera" CTA (home.cta.openCamera, en.json:731; HomeScreen.tsx:742-744, 1054-1066). The camera screen has a shutter, a gallery icon button (a11y "Choose from gallery", ScanCameraScreen.tsx:525-541) and a "Compare" CTA once two photos are taken (home.camera.compareCta, en.json:962; ScanCameraScreen.tsx:436-445).
findings.fix: Replace step 3 with: "Photos: tap the Scan tab, then \"Turn on camera\" (first time; allow camera access) or \"Open camera\". Photograph two products with the shutter button, then tap Compare." (see ready_text step 5).

findings.title: Gallery label is "Or pick from gallery", and it only shows before camera access
findings.claim: Packet line 285: "\"Pick from gallery\" selects photos from the library instead".
findings.evidence: home.camera.gallery "Pick from gallery" (en.json:964) is not used in src. The visible text link is home.permission.gallery_link "Or pick from gallery" (en.json:716). It renders only on the no-camera-permission card on Home (HomeScreen.tsx:767-774) and on ScanCamera (ScanCameraScreen.tsx:336-346). Once permission is granted, the gallery entry is an icon button next to the shutter (ScanCameraScreen.tsx:533-541). Picking needs two photos (MAX_IMAGES = 2, HomeScreen.tsx:97). One photo shows "Pick two photos" (HomeScreen.tsx:695-705).
findings.fix: Use: "To use library photos instead, tap the photo button next to the shutter (or \"Or pick from gallery\" before camera access is granted) and select two photos."

findings.title: Home opens in Scan mode, so the reviewer must tap Type before typing
findings.claim: Packet line 284: "On Home, type two products ... then tap Compare".
findings.evidence: Home starts with useState<InputMode>('scan') (HomeScreen.tsx:116). The two text boxes and their Compare button render only in the Type/Link modes, through TwoInputShell (HomeScreen.tsx:847-866; TwoInputShell.tsx:616-619, label home.compare.cta "Compare", en.json:729). The home tab is labelled "MYEZ" (App.tsx:140, app.name), not "Home".
findings.fix: Step 1 of ready_text: "On the MYEZ tab (home), the comparison card has three tabs: Scan (selected by default), Link and Type. Tap Type, enter ... then tap Compare."

findings.title: AI permission sheet: strings correct, gating confirmed on every compare path
findings.claim: Packet line 283: before the first comparison or scan, a one-time sheet titled "Your comparison is written with AI" with "Agree and continue" appears, and without it no comparison runs.
findings.evidence:
Title, body and Agree button come from aiConsent.title / aiConsent.body / aiConsent.agree (en.json:701-705; AiConsentSheet.tsx:83-124). The body names OpenAI and the training use, and ends "Your name, email and account details are not sent." Every Home entry is wrapped in withAiConsent:
- text compare: HomeScreen.tsx:373
- URL compare: :534
- Open camera CTA: :725-727
- camera-permission request, before the OS prompt: :731-735
- gallery fallback: :736-740
- scan preview rows: :779
- trending rows, through handleTextCompare: :666-673

ScanCamera is reachable only from Home (only navigate('ScanCamera') sites: HomeScreen.tsx:719, :779). Consent is stored per account per device under @qaren_ai_consent_<userId> (aiConsent.ts:9-15, 107-112), so a fresh account on the reviewer's device sees it once. "Not now" drops the action (aiConsent.ts:104-112).

Caveat: canCompare is checked before consent (HomeScreen.tsx:366-373), so an account already at its limit sees the limit screen first. This does not apply to premium accounts (useComparisonCounter.ts canCompare = isPremium || ...).
findings.fix: Keep the sentence, moved after the Compare tap in ready_text step 2. Reword it to "starts a comparison, the camera or the photo picker" so it matches the gated entry points.

findings.title: Account deletion path confirmed, with exact labels
findings.claim: Packet line 290: Profile tab -> gear icon (top right) -> Delete account (bottom of Edit Profile) -> confirm.
findings.evidence: The Profile tab is labelled "Profile" (App.tsx:160). The header gear (Settings icon, a11y label "Settings") navigates to EditProfile (ProfileScreen.tsx:333-342). EditProfile is a modal (App.tsx EditProfile screen, presentation modal). Its last block is the eyebrow "Account actions" with the row "Delete account" (EditProfileScreen.tsx:259-281; en.json:926, 930). The alert has title "Delete account", message "Are you sure? This cannot be undone." and buttons "Cancel" / "Delete account" (EditProfileScreen.tsx:127-136; en.json:354, 383). On confirm the app calls DELETE /api/v1/auth/account, clears consent, history and the session, then returns to sign-in (EditProfileScreen.tsx:137-150; App.tsx onAccountDeleted=handleLogout).
findings.fix: Use the exact path: "Profile tab -> gear icon (top right, labelled Settings) -> Edit Profile screen -> scroll to \"Account actions\" -> \"Delete account\" -> tap \"Delete account\" again in the confirmation."

findings.title: "Raised daily comparison limit" is false until the owner sets subscription_tier = 'premium'
findings.claim: Packet line 280: "Both review accounts have a raised daily comparison limit."
findings.evidence:
How the tier is stored:
- Column: public.users.subscription_tier TEXT DEFAULT 'free' (migrations/011_security_completion_freemium.sql:28).
- New users are inserted with 'free' (auth_service.py:405-409, 827-832).
- No CHECK constraint, FK or enum on the column in any repo migration. The live constraint is UNVERIFIED; run the read-only query below.

Limits:
- TIER_LIMITS (usage_service.py:138-149): free = lifetime_free 3, daily 3, monthly 10; premium = daily 10, monthly 70.
- An unknown value falls back to free (usage_service.py:355).

No tier cache:
- On every compare, consume_comparison_credit reads the tier straight from public.users through _get_user_tier_info (usage_service.py:350-355, 520-531). The same read serves /usage/status (:719-723).
- No Redis or LRU cache of the tier exists in app/; grep finds none.
- Only the usage counters live in Redis, keyed usage:daily:<id>:<UTC date> and usage:monthly:<id>:<UTC month> (usage_service.py:152-159).

Client:
- useComparisonCounter fetches /usage/status once per Home mount (useComparisonCounter.ts, effect with [] deps).
- isPremium makes canCompare always true on the client; the server still enforces 10 a day and 70 a month.

All three compare routes call consume_comparison_credit: text_routes.py:617/833/1019, url_routes.py:74, image_routes.py:289.
findings.fix:
Owner, Supabase SQL editor, after both accounts are registered, email-confirmed and onboarded:

-- A. read-only check (expect 2 rows, tier 'free', preferences_completed true)
SELECT id, email, subscription_tier, preferences_completed FROM public.users WHERE lower(email) IN (lower('<REVIEW EMAIL 1>'), lower('<REVIEW EMAIL 2>'));
-- B. read-only: any live constraint on the column (expect 0 rows)
SELECT conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'public.users'::regclass AND pg_get_constraintdef(oid) ILIKE '%subscription_tier%';
-- C. raise both (expect exactly 2 rows back, both 'premium')
UPDATE public.users SET subscription_tier = 'premium' WHERE lower(email) IN (lower('<REVIEW EMAIL 1>'), lower('<REVIEW EMAIL 2>')) RETURNING id, email, subscription_tier;

Caching caveats:
1. No tier cache exists, so the server applies the change on the very next compare.
2. An already-open app keeps its old canCompare and counter until Home remounts. Sign out and back in, or force-quit and relaunch.
3. The Redis day/month counters are not reset. Compares the owner runs on these accounts (warm-up, onboarding check) count toward the 10 per day until the UTC day rolls over (03:00 Bahrain time). Do the warm-up with a different account.
4. Deleting an account resets its tier to 'free' (migration 043:141, :208). Account 2 is the spare.

After step C, the notes sentence "raised limit of 10 comparisons per day" becomes true.

findings.title: Sign in with Apple needs the consent checkbox first and leads into onboarding
findings.claim: Packet line 280: "Sign in with Apple is also available; it creates a new account with the standard free allowance."
findings.evidence: The native Apple button shows on iOS when available (LoginScreen.tsx:212-215, 426-440), with label auth.appleSignIn "Continue with Apple" (en.json:368). handleAppleSignIn returns early with a consent error unless the checkbox "I am 13 or older and I agree to the ..." is ticked (LoginScreen.tsx:261-268; en.json:999-1001). A first Apple sign-in inserts a public.users row with tier 'free' (auth_service.py:827-832). The free allowance is 3 lifetime-free compares that also bump the daily counter, so 3 on day one, then 3 a day and 10 a month (usage_service.py:138-143, 359-377). A new account has preferences_completed false, so App.tsx shows onboarding before Main (App.tsx needsPreferences branch). The new flow is on at 100% (features.ts:30, 108-110), and for a signed-in user it runs 16 screens with step 16 skipped (OnboardingFlow.tsx:128-131, 208-219, 348-350). These are required: language, country, 1-3 priorities, budget, brand attitude, attribution (OnboardingFlow.tsx:169-191). The last screen offers "Allow notifications" / "Maybe later" (en.json:689-690).
findings.fix: Use the ready_text paragraph: tick the checkbox first; the free allowance is 3 a day and 10 a month; a new account answers a 16-screen first-run questionnaire before Home, with the required answers listed.

findings.title: Google sign-in button ships in build 2; whether it works is unverified
findings.claim: Packet line 293: add "Google sign-in is also available." only if the GOO device check passes.
findings.evidence: LoginScreen.tsx:441-449 always renders SocialButton "Continue with Google" (auth.googleSignIn, en.json:367). It is gated by the same consent checkbox (LoginScreen.tsx:229-233). @react-native-google-signin/google-signin is a dependency (package.json) and is configured in app.json:226-228. This audit did not test it on a device. A reviewer will see and may tap the button whatever the notes say, so a broken Google flow is a guideline 2.1 rejection risk even if the sentence is left out.
findings.fix: Owner: test Continue with Google on build 2 (TestFlight) before Add for Review. If it works, the notes may add "Continue with Google is also available (same checkbox)." If it fails, fix it before submitting; the notes cannot cover a visible broken button.

findings.title: Bahrain market and BHD confirmed; "retailers across the GCC" is unsupported
findings.claim: Packet line 288: "Prices are in Bahraini Dinar (BHD), gathered from retailers across the GCC, and change over time."
findings.evidence:
Every compare request hardcodes region 'bahrain':
- text REST: api.ts:681 and :971
- stream: :824
- image: :258 and :302
- vision path: HomeScreen.tsx:562

The backend maps bahrain to BHD (exchange_rate_service.py:99; extraction_service.py:89; structured_comparison_service.py:1291). This audit found nothing showing the price sources are GCC-wide; the clause is UNVERIFIED.
findings.fix: Use: "Market: results use the Bahrain market. Prices are shown in Bahraini Dinar (BHD) and change over time."

findings.title: No in-app purchases, subscriptions, ads or tracking in the binary
findings.claim: "This version has no in-app purchases, subscriptions or ads, and does not track users."
findings.evidence: package.json dependencies list no StoreKit, react-native-iap, expo-in-app-purchases, RevenueCat, AdMob, Facebook, AppsFlyer, Firebase or Amplitude package (git show 7b224c5a:SmartCompareApp/package.json). app.json has no NSUserTrackingUsageDescription and declares NSPrivacyTracking false (app.json:26) with NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeTracking false on every type (app.json:31-92). git grep for these names in src finds nothing. PaywallScreen only shows limit and refresh copy plus Done (PaywallScreen.tsx:100-176; en.json:373-381); nothing is sold. trackEvent posts first-party events to the app's own API (api.ts:1023). The live privacy policy says "We do not show third-party ads and we do not track you across other companies' apps" (GET /api/v1/legal/privacy, 200).
findings.fix: Keep the sentence. Optionally add "The daily-limit screen only explains when free comparisons refresh; nothing is sold." so the word "Paywall" a reviewer may meet is explained.

findings.title: "20-40 seconds" matches canary 7c, but it is one pair, and live health shows event-loop stalls
findings.claim: "A comparison usually takes 20-40 seconds".
findings.evidence: Canary 7c PASS (ledger.md:47 at 7b224c5a), pair iPhone 15 vs Samsung Galaxy S24 with the PHASE2 guard and UNIFIED_SEARCH_BOUND on: q compare 26.9 s, pair compare 28.2 s, probe 30.0 s, stream 32.4 s. Live GET /health just now returned 200 with loop_lag_max_60s_ms 10805 and loop_lag_max_ms 14802, so a stall could push one compare past 40 s.
findings.fix: Keep "usually 20-40 seconds". Use a warm-up READY pair for <PAIR A>/<PAIR B> on the review day.

findings.title: Bright Data returns 401 live: some prices may show "No confirmed price yet."
findings.claim: "... and a price for each product when one is found."
findings.evidence: GET https://web-production-58776.up.railway.app/health returned brightdata_auth {last_status: 401, at: 2026-10-11T15:55:27Z}. Canary 7c already had the second product at 1/2 prices (ledger.md:47). The empty-price copy is results.price.pending "No confirmed price yet." (en.json:155). The sentence is hedged, so it stays true, but a reviewer may see missing prices.
findings.fix: Owner: renew the Bright Data token (docs/runbooks/brightdata-token-renewal.md), then rerun the warm-up to pick the READY pair. The notes now name the empty-price state so it does not read as a bug.

findings.title: Notes omit email confirmation for new email accounts
findings.claim: The notes do not say what a reviewer who registers a new email account will see.
findings.evidence: Register handles a confirmation-required sign-up with "Check your inbox ... Confirm your email, then sign in." (en.json:865-867). Login's error copy also points to confirmation (en.json:1009). Whether production Supabase requires email confirmation is UNVERIFIED (no dashboard access). Packet line 437 says "confirm email if required".
findings.fix: Add: "New email accounts (Sign Up) may be asked to confirm the email address through a link before signing in."

findings.title: Sign in with Apple tokens are not revoked on account deletion
findings.claim: Packet section 5 records SIWA token revocation as U11 = A (after launch).
findings.evidence: The delete path calls only DELETE /api/v1/auth/account (EditProfileScreen.tsx:137-150). Apple's account-deletion guidance for apps that offer Sign in with Apple expects token revocation. The Apple page was not fetched in this audit (UNVERIFIED wording). This is not a notes sentence, but a reviewer who tests deletion with an Apple account can raise it.
findings.fix: Accept the known risk (owner ruling U11 = A), or schedule the backend revocation before submission. Do not claim revocation in the notes.

findings.title: Sign-in and contact fields are consistent with the build
findings.claim: Packet lines 260-270: Sign-in required Yes; user name and password = review account 1; contact name, +973 phone and a monitored email.
findings.evidence: App.tsx shows only the Auth stack until isAuthenticated, so every feature needs sign-in. Login takes an email and password and submits with "Sign In" (LoginScreen.tsx:526-532; en.json:366). The support@getmyez.com and privacy@getmyez.com routing works (orchestrator context). The phone-format rule is quoted in the packet from Apple's help page; it was not re-fetched here.
findings.fix: Use a monitored inbox, for example support@getmyez.com, as the contact email. Enter the phone as +973 followed by the number.

result.ready_text:
Sign-in is required: the account holds the user's comparison history, preferences and comparison allowance. The app opens on the sign-in screen.

Review account 1: <REVIEW EMAIL 1> / <REVIEW PASSWORD 1>
Review account 2 (spare, in case account 1 is deleted): <REVIEW EMAIL 2> / <REVIEW PASSWORD 2>
Enter the email and password and tap Sign In. Both review accounts have already completed the first-run questions and have a raised limit of 10 comparisons per day.

Sign in with Apple ("Continue with Apple") is also available: first tick the box "I am 13 or older and I agree to the Terms...". It creates a new account with the standard free allowance (3 comparisons a day, 10 a month). A new account first answers a short first-run questionnaire (16 screens; language, country, 1-3 priorities, budget, brand preference and how you heard of us must be chosen, the other screens only need Continue, and the notifications screen offers "Maybe later").

How to test:
1. On the MYEZ tab (home), the comparison card has three tabs: Scan (selected by default), Link and Type. Tap Type, enter "<PAIR A>" and "<PAIR B>" (a pair that passed our check today), then tap Compare.
2. The first time an account starts a comparison, the camera or the photo picker on a device, the app shows a one-time sheet "Your comparison is written with AI" that names OpenAI and explains what is sent. Tap "Agree and continue". "Not now" cancels; comparisons cannot run without this agreement.
3. A comparison usually takes 20-40 seconds while we gather specs, reviews and prices.
4. Results show the winner, the reasons, "Where the runner-up wins", and a price for each product when one is found (otherwise "No confirmed price yet.").
5. Photos: tap the Scan tab, then "Turn on camera" (first time; allow camera access) or "Open camera". Photograph two products with the shutter button, then tap Compare. To use library photos instead, tap the photo button next to the shutter (or "Or pick from gallery" before camera access is granted) and select two photos.
6. Link compares two product page links, for example from Amazon or Noon.

Market: results use the Bahrain market. Prices are shown in Bahraini Dinar (BHD) and change over time.
AI processing: the product names, links (with the text of those pages), photos and the profile preferences named on the permission sheet are sent to OpenAI to write the comparison. OpenAI may use these inputs and its outputs to evaluate and train its models; the permission sheet says so. The user's name, email and account details are not sent.
New email accounts (Sign Up) may be asked to confirm the email address through a link before signing in.
Account deletion: Profile tab -> gear icon (top right, labelled Settings) -> Edit Profile screen -> scroll to "Account actions" -> "Delete account" -> tap "Delete account" again in the confirmation.
This version has no in-app purchases, subscriptions or ads, and does not track users. The daily-limit screen only explains when free comparisons refresh; nothing is sold.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced. home.scan "Scan Product" (en.json:111) is not used as a bare key anywhere in src; only home.scan.preview.* keys are used (HomeScreen.tsx:787-838). Home shows Scan/Link/Type tabs (HomeScreen.tsx:1002-1038; en.json:710-712), "Turn on camera" when there is no camera permission (HomeScreen.tsx:758-774), and, once permission is granted, two "Tap to snap" rows plus the "Open camera" CTA (HomeScreen.tsx:779-844, 1055-1066). The finding leaves out the "Tap to snap" rows. I lowered the severity: a visible "Scan" tab exists, so a reviewer can still find the photo flow, and a wrong label in the notes is unlikely to cause a rejection on its own.

Reproduced. home.camera.gallery (en.json:964) is unused in src. The visible link is home.permission.gallery_link "Or pick from gallery" (en.json:716), shown only on the no-permission cards (HomeScreen.tsx:770-774; ScanCameraScreen.tsx:336-346). After permission is granted, the gallery entry is an icon with no visible text (ScanCameraScreen.tsx:533-541, a11y "Choose from gallery" en.json:969). The fix text is wrong, though. The icon button calls onGalleryPick, which picks ONE photo per tap into the next empty slot (ScanCameraScreen.tsx:209-231), so "select two photos" is inaccurate for that path. I lowered the severity because this is a one-word label difference.

Reproduced. useState<InputMode>('scan') at HomeScreen.tsx:116, with no restore of a saved mode. TwoInputShell (the text boxes and Compare) renders only outside scan mode (HomeScreen.tsx:847-866). The home tab label is t('app.name') = "MYEZ" (App.tsx:140; en.json:2). I lowered the severity from high because the Type tab is visibly labelled one tap away; the notes mislead but do not block review.

Confirmed.
- Strings: en.json:701-705.
- withAiConsent wraps text compare (HomeScreen.tsx:373), URL compare (:534), the Open camera CTA (:725-727), the camera-permission request (:731-735), the gallery fallback (:736-740) and the preview rows (:779).
- The only navigate('ScanCamera') sites are HomeScreen.tsx:719 and :779.
- The other navigate('Results') sites pass comparison_id, which opens history and runs no new compare (HistoryScreen.tsx:787/796, ProfileScreen.tsx:412).
- Consent is stored per user (aiConsent.ts:9-15, 114-119).
- The canCompare check comes before consent (HomeScreen.tsx:366-373).
- Client isPremium makes canCompare true (useComparisonCounter.ts:69-82).

Confirmed.
- The gear navigates to EditProfile with a11y label "Settings" (ProfileScreen.tsx:334-342).
- The "Account actions" eyebrow and the "Delete account" row: EditProfileScreen.tsx:259-281.
- Alert title, message and buttons: EditProfileScreen.tsx:127-136 (en.json:354, 383, 930).
- On confirm: DELETE /api/v1/auth/account, then clearAiConsent, clearRecentSearches and clearSession (:137-148).

One nit on the fix text: "Settings" is only an accessibility label with no visible text, so "labelled Settings" may mislead a sighted reviewer.

Reproduced.
- TIER_LIMITS: free daily 3 / monthly 10 / lifetime_free 3; premium daily 10 / monthly 70 (usage_service.py:138-149).
- The tier is read from users on every consume (usage_service.py:350-355, 520-531) and on status (:719-723).
- The column is TEXT DEFAULT 'free' (migrations/011:28), and no CHECK constraint appears in the repo migrations.
- Deletion resets the tier to 'free' (migration 043:141, :208).

I lowered the severity from high: the packet already makes this step an owner prerequisite. Line 437 says "`users.subscription_tier = premium` in the Supabase table editor", and line 273 says to paste the notes only after the demo accounts exist. The sentence is a gated prerequisite, not an unplanned defect. The SQL is a useful sharpening.

Confirmed.
- handleAppleSignIn returns early without the checkbox (LoginScreen.tsx:258-268), and so does Google (:229-233).
- The Apple button shows only on iOS when available (:212-216, 426-437).
- CANARY_NEW_ONBOARDING_PERCENT = 100 is in the build (features.ts:30).

- Step 17 has "Allow notifications" / "Maybe later" (Step17Notifications.tsx:146,156; en.json:689-690).

Confirmed.
- The Google SocialButton renders unconditionally (LoginScreen.tsx:441-449).
- The dependency @react-native-google-signin/google-signin ^16.1.2 is in package.json.

The Bahrain/BHD part is confirmed: api.ts:681, :824, :971 and HomeScreen.tsx:562 hardcode region 'bahrain'. The WRONG status is overstated, though. The backend does query non-Bahrain GCC retailers: uae.sharafdg.com (AED), danube.sa (SAR) and nahdionline.com (SAR) in algolia_service.py:107-128, and extraction_service.py:930 cites "Major GCC retailers (Noon, Jarir, Extra, Sharaf DG, LuLu)". They are marked genuine:False, and the audit did not show whether they feed displayed prices. The clause is UNVERIFIED rather than shown false. The finding's safer wording is still fine as an edit.

Confirmed.

- app.json:26 has NSPrivacyTracking false. NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeTracking is false 13 times and true 0 times, and there is no NSUserTrackingUsageDescription.

- Live /api/v1/legal/privacy returned 200.

Confirmed. ledger.md:47 at 7b224c5a records canary 7c PASS: q 26.9 s, pair 28.2 s, probe 30.0 s, stream 32.4 s, second product at 1/2 prices. My live GET /health returned 200 with loop_lag_max_ms 14802 and loop_lag_max_60s_ms 6546 (it was 10805 in the finding, so the value fluctuates), and the stall caveat holds.

Reproduced. My live GET /health returned brightdata_auth {last_status: 401, at: 2026-10-11T15:55:27Z}. Canary 7c's second product had no price (ledger.md:47). results.price.pending "No confirmed price yet." is en.json:155.

Confirmed. The copy exists: register.emailConfirmation.* (en.json:865-866) and auth.errors.invalidCredentials (en.json:1009). Whether production requires email confirmation is UNVERIFIED, and the packet (line 437) says "confirm email if required". The added hedge sentence is accurate.

critic.summary:
I ran a completeness pass over the three audited dimensions (review notes, listing and URLs, review risk). Everything below was checked read-only at 7b224c5a, plus GET-only checks against the allowed live hosts. `git diff --stat eed0f628 7b224c5a -- SmartCompareApp app landing` is empty, so the source at 7b224c5a is the binary under review.

**Gaps nobody covered:**
- **Over-the-air (OTA) update channel (C1, high, unverified).** Build 2 runs on runtime 1.0.0 and the `production` channel, with expo-updates checking for updates on every launch. Nobody has confirmed that the production channel serves no update. A stale bundle there would replace the reviewed code on the reviewer's phone.
- **Forgot password (C2, medium).** The recovery email lands on the API host, because Supabase's Site URL is the API host and `ENABLE_PASSWORD_RESET_DEEP_LINK` is still off. The in-app reset screen is already in build 2.
- **"25+ retailers" claim (C6, medium).** It shows during every compare, on onboarding step 3 and in the results tips. It comes from a design mock and was never measured.
- **Required "Where did you hear about us?" (C7, medium).** New accounts (for example Sign in with Apple) cannot skip this marketing question. It sits badly with guideline 5.1.1(v) and (iii).
- **Third-party content, guideline 5.2.2 (C8, medium).** Nobody audited it, and the corrected review notes now name Amazon and Noon.
- **Supabase free plan (C10, medium).** Its spend cap and read-only risk during review are not covered by R4.
- **Mac and Vision Pro availability (C9, low).** iPhone apps are available on Apple Silicon Macs unless deselected, and the packet never mentions it.
- **Features missing from the notes (C12, low).** Guideline 2.3.1(a) wants every feature described; History, invites and bonus credits, sharing and notifications are not.

**Corrections to verified findings:**
- C3: Supabase "Confirm email" is measured OFF (S74 ledger:70). The review notes' email-confirmation sentence (F13) should be removed, not hedged.
- C11: live /health now shows `loop_lag_max_ms` 16190, up from 14802. Since that figure only ever rises, a new stall of at least 14.8 s happened after the R3 verifier's samples. That contradicts the verifier's "one stall since boot" reading.

**Unverified claims I closed:**
- C4: the live TLS chain (leaf, YE2, Root YE, X2, X1) matches the app's pinned keys today.
- C5: account deletion is a real full erasure in production (migration 043 POSTCHECK passed).

`ready_text` holds the extra pre-submission checklist.
